markets.title: Russia to Allow Gasoline Exports for Producers Through July
markets.description: Russia will allow gasoline exports for fuel producers through July 31, while extending a temporary ban for other suppliers.

markets.title: Dollar Rallies Most Since May as Trump Taps Warsh: Markets Wrap
markets.description: The biggest dollar rally since May accelerated a plunge in precious metals as President Donald Trump announced his pick for the Federal Reserve’s top job: Kevin Warsh, who’s seen as less supportive of deep rate cuts and more worried about inflation. Stocks fell. Bonds were mixed.

markets.title: Italy’s Outlook Raised to Positive by S&P in New Meloni Win
markets.description: Italy’s credit rating outlook was raised to positive from stable by S&P Global Ratings, the latest victory for Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni.

markets.title: Filmmaker Laura Poitras on US Actions in Venezuela
markets.description: "The US doesn't have the right to steal resources." BAFTA nominated filmmaker Laura Poitras tells Mishal Husain that US action in Venezuela amounts to regime change in pursuit of oil. Subscribe to The Mishal Husain Show wherever you get your podcasts. (Source: Bloomberg)

markets.title: Kazakhstan Starts Gradual Restoration of Output at Tengiz Field
markets.description: The Chevron-led venture Tengizchevroil has started to restore production at the Tengiz oil field, Kazakhstan’s largest, after operations were partially suspended earlier this month.

markets.title: India’s NSE Targets IPO in Seven to Eight Months, CNBC Says
markets.description: The National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. plans to launch its initial public offering in the next seven to eight months, CNBC-TV18 reported, citing Chief Executive Officer Ashish Kumar Chauhan.

markets.title: Philippine Regulator Charges Villar Land on Market Manipulation
markets.description: The Philippine market regulator has filed a criminal complaint against the property-holding firm of the country’s second-richest man, Manuel Villar.

markets.title: Africa’s Gambling Boom: Investment, Risk and Regulation
markets.description: Sports wagering is booming in Africa. Fueled by a young population, and access to latest technology, legal gambling revenues across the continent have nearly tripled in the past decade, turning it into a multi-billion-dollar market that global operators can no longer ignore. Bloomberg's Olatomiwa Babalola and Senior Africa reporter Loni Prinsloo explain. (Source: Bloomberg)

markets.title: China Factory Activity Unexpectedly Slides Into Contraction
markets.description: China’s factory activity unexpectedly worsened after snapping its worst contraction streak on record in December, as the world’s second-largest economy struggles to pick up momentum.

markets.title: CME Raises Gold, Silver Margins After Historic Price Plunge
markets.description: CME Group is raising margins on Comex gold and silver futures after prices suffered their biggest slides in decades.

markets.title: Trump Picks BLS Economist Brett Matsumoto to Head Agency
markets.description: President Donald Trump said he intends to nominate Brett Matsumoto to lead the Bureau of Labor Statistics, his second pick for the role that’s been vacant since August.

markets.title: Andreessen, Coinbase Directors Face Trading Suit for Now
markets.description: A Delaware judge ruled that a shareholder lawsuit alleging insider trading by several directors of Coinbase Global Inc., including venture capitalist Marc Andreessen, can proceed for now after an internal investigation cleared the defendants of wrongdoing.

markets.title: Market Swings in India Surge From Historic Low as Budget Nears
markets.description: Indian stocks are seeing a resurgence of volatility just weeks after being dubbed the world’s calmest equity market, with growing skepticism sparking an exodus of overseas investors.

markets.title: Stocks Lower as Commodities and Tech Weigh on S&P; Gold, Silver Dip | The Close 1/30/2026
markets.description: Bloomberg Television brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Federal Reserve Governor Stephen Miran, City University of New York’s Paul Krugman, Starbucks’ Brian Niccol, Wolfe Research’s Darrin Peller, TCW’s Bryan Whalen, University of Pennsylvania’s Peter Conti-Brown, Apollo’s Trosten Slok, Rep. Brad Sherman (D-CA), Former World Bank’s Paul Romer, Goldman Sachs’ Eric Sheridan. (Source: Bloomberg)

markets.title: AI Fears Hinder Deutsche Bank’s $1.2 Billion Loan Deal for Conga
markets.description: A group of lenders led by Deutsche Bank AG is at risk of getting stuck with about $1.2 billion of loans linked to the acquisition of an artificial intelligence-driven software provider, as investors shy away from businesses perceived as vulnerable to competition from free AI tools.

markets.title: Fmr World Bank Chief Economist: Trump Doesn’t Believe in Fed Independence
markets.description: Paul Romer, Nobel laureate, former World Bank chief economist, and Boston College professor, says Donald Trump does not believe in central bank independence. Speaking with Romaine Bostick and Katie Greifeld on The Close, Romer says it is entirely possible Trump could move to impose wage and price controls. (Source: Bloomberg)

markets.title: Brazil’s Haddad Pitches Ministry Ally for Open Central Bank Seat
markets.description: Brazil Finance Minister Fernando Haddad has pitched President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on naming an ally from inside his ministry to an open seat on the central bank board, according to two people with knowledge of the situation.

markets.title: Oil Rally Runs Out of Steam After Trump Says Iran Wants a Deal
markets.description: Oil edged lower, though still notched its biggest monthly gain since 2022, as US President Donald Trump reiterated openness to negotiations with Iran though investors remain on edge about the potential for further tensions. West Texas Intermediate fell 0.3% to settle near $65 a barrel, snapping a breathless three-day rally, while Brent ended the day above $70. Prices tumbled after Trump told reporters that Iran wants to make a deal. The US president’s messaging has shifted from punishing Tehran for its deadly crackdown on protesters to this week trying to extract a new nuclear agreement. Dr. Ellen Wald, President of Transversal Consulting, Senior Fellow at the Atlantic Council, and author of "Saudi, Inc." joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss. She also weighs in on Chevron and Exxon earnings results. Wald speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

markets.title: Bowman Says Fed Can 'Afford to Take Time' With Rate Cuts
markets.description: Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman says she saw merit in waiting to lower rates further given elevated inflation and uncertainty over potential distortions in economic data during an event in Oahu, Hawaii. (This report is audio only.) (Source: Bloomberg)

markets.title: Rep. Sherman (D-CA): Investigation into Fed is ‘Phony’
markets.description: Rep. Brad Sherman (D-CA) calls the Fed investigation a “phony” attempt to intimidate the central bank. Speaking with Romaine Bostick and Katie Greifeld on The Close, he says Kevin Warsh backs a digital dollar to compete with crypto. (Source: Bloomberg)

technology.title: Nvidia Investment in OpenAI Round ‘Nothing Like’ $100 Billion
technology.description: Nvidia Corp. will “absolutely” be involved in OpenAI’s current funding round, though the investment will be “nothing like” $100 billion, Chief Executive Jensen Huang said.

technology.title: Elon Musk’s Relentless AI Pursuit Has Him on the Hunt for Capital

technology.title: Tesla Bulls and Bears Agree: This Is Not an Auto Stock

Plus, Apple reports record sales but the rising cost of memory worries investors. And, SpaceX is said to be considering a merger with Tesla or xAI. (Source: Bloomberg)

technology.title: Eurizon’s Jen Says ‘Bumpy Road’ Is Ideal Path to Weaker Dollar
technology.description: The ideal path to a weaker dollar from the perspective of US officials may involve a “bumpy road” with a series of lurches, rather than a steady decline, according to Stephen Jen at Eurizon SLJ Capital.

technology.title: Apple Gives Upbeat Forecast, Warns of Rising Costs
technology.description: Apple delivered record quarterly sales over the holiday season and forecast continued strong demand, but the company also warned about the impact of the rising costs of components. technology.title: Minnesota Woman Says Her Global Entry Nixed After Agent Run-In
technology.description: A payments director at the Minneapolis-based retail giant Target Corp. said her fast-track credentials for airport security were revoked following an interaction with a federal border patrol agent who claimed he had facial recognition and was recording with a “body cam.”

technology.title: Metal Parts Startup Raises $220M Led By Eclipse, 1789 Capital
technology.description: Metal parts maker VulcanForms has closed a $220 million funding round, led by existing investor Eclipse and 1789 Capital, where Donald Trump Jr. is a partner. The company, which uses additive manufacturing, is part of a growing wave of startups using advances in technology to bring manufacturing back to the US. VulcanForms CEO Kevin Kassekert joins Caroline Hyde and Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech.” (Source: Bloomberg)

technology.title: Apple Has Watched AI From the Stands Says Dan Ives
technology.description: Apple Inc. enjoyed a sharp rebound in China during the holiday period, when demand for the new iPhone 17 fueled its first $25 billion quarter in the region since the end of 2021. The company generated sales of $25.5 billion from its greater China segment during a three-month span that ended Dec. 27. The revenue soared 38%, smashing Wall Street’s average estimate of $21.8 billion and far outpacing total sales growth. Dan Ives, Global Head of Technology Research at Wedbush Securities joins to discuss on Bloomberg Intelligence. (Source: Bloomberg)

technology.title: Apple Loses More AI Researchers and a Siri Executive in Latest Departures
technology.description: Apple Inc. has lost at least four more of its artificial intelligence researchers in recent weeks in addition to a top Siri executive, with the staff headed to employers such as Meta Platforms Inc. and Google DeepMind.

Critics who see them as a license for landlords to rip off their tenants have convinced the Labour government to overhaul the system. Here’s why campaign groups have called it an “end of history moment.”

industries.title: Cockpit Voice Recorders Must Retain 25 Hours of Data Under New FAA Rule
industries.description: New aircraft must have a cockpit voice recorder that can retain 25 hours of information under a final rule from US aviation regulators intended to improve safety and help investigators determine causes of accidents.

industries.title: French Health Startup Alan in Funding Talks at €5 Billion Value
industries.description: Alan is in talks to raise funds at a €5 billion ($5.9 billion) valuation as the French health-insurance startup works to expand its customer base, people familiar with the matter said.

industries.title: Amex Nears Deal for Last Office Tower at World Trade Center Site
industries.description: American Express Co. is close to a deal to relocate its headquarters to 2 World Trade Center, a move that would allow Silverstein Properties to start construction of the long-planned Manhattan skyscraper, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

industries.title: Deutsche Bank Faces Other AML Probe, German Prosecutors Confirm
industries.description: Deutsche Bank AG’s money-laundering raids by prosecutors this week were sparked by another, previously unreported probe, authorities said on Friday, confirming comments by Chief Financial Officer James von Moltke.
